Sāyaṇa: sarvaṃ parva ... samṛdham eva avikalāvayavam eva bhavati, ivaśabdo 'vadhāraṇe, gharmakāle mṛdbhāvam āpannā maṇḍūkāḥ punar varṣaṇe saty avikalāṅgāḥ prādurbhavanti: the 'iva' is emphatic (so 'truly', against Griffith’s 'seems'), the limbs are whole, the frogs turned to clay in the hot season appear whole when rain falls. The paraphrase carries exactly this, no drift; Wilson’s note ('says the scholiast') confirms it is Sāyaṇa’s. verse.js ok (7.103.5 at [618,5]); entry-check ok. Plain sense checked on day.js: 7.103 praises the frogs whose voice Parjanya inspires at the first of the rains (v1, v7), and v5 is where the hymn first moves into the second person ('Your', 'ye'); accurate and no more. No Yāska on this verse (packet). No school, comparison or tone issue.
